passage: "Dilnaz, got a minute? Just us." "If it's about the rent, I'll pay Monday." "It's not the rent. You've skipped dinner all week. You cancelled the film, and the birthday." "I'm busy, Sharmila." "And yesterday you said, 'What's the point of any of it.' I keep thinking about that." "It was a joke. Don't lecture me." "I won't. I'm not here to fix anything. I just miss you, and I'm worried." A long silence. Dilnaz picks at her sleeve. "Everything's just... heavy. All the time." "Okay. Thank you for telling me. I'm staying right here." "I don't know what to do." "Would you see the campus counsellor? I can book it with you, right now. I'll walk you there." "...Only if you come." "I'm coming."

qa.q: What did Dilnaz cancel, according to Sharmila?
How does Sharmila feel about the changes she has noticed in Dilnaz?
qa.a: She feels worried and misses Dilnaz, saying so plainly, and keeps thinking about the remark 'What's the point of any of it.'

qa.q: Which of Sharmila's choices helped Dilnaz open up?
qa.a: Sharmila checked in privately, named what was noticed, promised not to lecture, and simply stayed.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz see Sharmila's offer to walk with her?
qa.a: She may feel less alone and more able to go, since she agrees only if Sharmila comes.

grounding: Sharmila notices missed meals, cancelled plans and dark remarks, checks in privately, listens and stays present, and gently encourages professional help.

passage: I'm Tenzin. Last year my roommate Jagdish slowly disappeared in front of me, and I almost didn't notice. First it was meals. He'd say he'd eaten, but his plate stayed clean in the rack. Then he pulled out of the trek we'd planned for months. Then the remarks: "Nothing I do matters anyway." I laughed the first time. I'm not proud of that. The third time, I shut the door and sat on his bed. "You don't have to talk. But I've noticed you're not eating, and I'm worried about you." He didn't say anything for a long time. Then he said, "I'm so tired of feeling like this." I didn't try to fix it. I just stayed. Over the next week I kept asking gently, and in the end he let me go with him to the college doctor.

qa.q: What trip did Jagdish pull out of?
qa.a: The trek they had planned for months.

qa.q: How did Tenzin feel by the third remark, and what shows it?
qa.a: Tenzin was worried about Jagdish; Tenzin shut the door, sat on his bed and said, 'I'm worried about you.'

qa.q: What did Tenzin do after the third remark that helped?
qa.a: Tenzin shut the door, spoke privately, named the worry, stayed without trying to fix it, and later went with him to the doctor.

qa.q: How might Jagdish have felt when Tenzin laughed at the first remark?
qa.a: He may have felt unheard and more alone, which could have made it harder to speak up.

grounding: A roommate recalls noticing missed meals, cancelled plans and dark remarks, checking in privately, staying present and encouraging professional help.
